problem_text:
A logistics company must coordinate a fleet of drones to perform maintenance checks at six distinct cellular network towers spread across a region.  
The towers are positioned at these GPS coordinates:  
Tower Alpha: (111,46)  
Tower Beta: (15,128)  
Tower Gamma: (119,10)  
Tower Delta: (152,25)  
Tower Epsilon: (179,100)  
Tower Zeta: (51,66)  

The flight distances between towers, measured in kilometers, are as follows:  
Alpha to Gamma: 36.9 km  
Alpha to Delta: 46.1 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 86.8 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 63.2 km  
Beta to Gamma: 157.3 km  
Beta to Delta: 171.4 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 166.4 km  
Beta to Zeta: 71.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 36.2 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 108.2 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 88.1 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 79.7 km  
Delta to Zeta: 109.0 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 132.4 km  

Due to restricted airspace, no direct flight path exists between Tower Alpha and Tower Beta.  
Additionally, operational rules mandate that exactly one of the following two flight corridors must be part of the inspection circuit: the corridor between Beta and Gamma, or the corridor between Gamma and Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total flight distance for a closed-loop route that visits each tower precisely once and returns to the origin tower.
